PAPERS.title: Short-term health impacts of air pollution in Canada: a nonlinear multi-pollutant Bayesian case-crossover framework.
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, NO2 and O3 from imputed fixed-site monitoring, jointly modelled with nonlinear exposure-response
PAPERS.n: Cause-specific daily mortality 2001-2015 and hospitalisation 2001-2018 across 20 Census Divisions covering over half of Canada's population. A 10-unit contrast in the combined PM2.5+NO2 metric gave +1.5% non-accidental mortality (95% CrI 0.3 to 2.2), +0.6% hospitalisation (0.0 to 1.3) and +2.7% senior respiratory hospitalisation (0.9 to 4.5). Several PM2.5 and NO2 curves were nonlinear; O3 was near-linear. The methodological gain is real: exposure uncertainty from imputation is propagated rather than ignored, and CD-level curves are partially pooled. The threat is interpretive: a summed PM2.5+NO2 index has no single-pollutant counterpart, so the coefficient cannot be dropped into a PM2.5-only burden model, and the CrIs for cause- and age-specific strata are wide. For sensing: imputed monitor gaps are treated as an exposure-error source, which is exactly where dense low-cost networks would shrink the posterior.

PAPERS.title: The role and management of dietary and environmental factors in pediatric atopic dermatitis.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM2.5 dichotomised at 35 ug/m3 (source and averaging period not stated)
PAPERS.n: Stage 1: 535 paediatric atopic-dermatitis cases diagnosed 2022-2024 and 535 age- and sex-matched controls, conditional logistic regression. PM2.5 above 35 ug/m3 carried an adjusted OR of 2.48 (95% CI 1.80 to 3.50), alongside early milk/egg sensitisation (3.18), winter indoor humidity below 40% (1.92) and S. aureus colonisation above 50% (4.08). Stage 2 was a 66-child non-randomised intervention comparison on diet and home care, with no air-quality component. The PM estimate is the weakest element: the exposure source, spatial resolution and averaging window are not given, a single dichotomy at 35 ug/m3 discards the gradient, and matched hospital controls invite selection on healthcare use. Treat the OR as hypothesis-grade. Relevance to sensing is indirect - indoor humidity and PM2.5 are measured by the same low-cost units, so a home-sensor design could separate them properly.

PAPERS.title: The Effect of Synbiotic Supplementation on Malondialdehyde Levels in Adolescents Exposed to Air Pollution: A Randomized, Single-Blind, Controlled Clinical Trial.
PAPERS.pm: Residence in a polluted setting; no individual PM measurement reported
PAPERS.n: Seventy healthy 10-18-year-olds randomised, single-blind, to synbiotics (n = 38) or omega-3 (n = 32) for 8 weeks; outcome serum malondialdehyde. MDA fell within the synbiotic arm (148.8 to 51.5), but the between-arm difference was null (P = 0.75); only after covariate adjustment did synbiotic use associate with MDA reduction. That is the result that matters, and it is null on the pre-specified contrast. The comparator is an active antioxidant, so the trial cannot test synbiotics against nothing; there is no placebo, no measured exposure and the MDA standard deviations exceed the post-treatment mean. It cannot inform a PM dose-response. Carried because nutritional mitigation of PM oxidative stress keeps recurring in the trial registry; an exposure-stratified design using personal sensors is what this line of work lacks.

PAPERS.title: Impacts of PM2.5 air pollution on high-skilled worker productivity in China.
PAPERS.pm: Annual city-level ambient PM2.5 (mean 45.9 ug/m3), instrumented
PAPERS.n: Individual scholars' publication counts linked to annual PM2.5 at their city, with an instrumental-variable design. Each 1 ug/m3 rise in annual PM2.5 reduced publications by 0.23% (95% CI -0.28% to -0.17%); scaled nationally, a 1% PM2.5 rise costs about 1,053 papers. Effects were larger in heavy-pollution years and among younger, more productive scholars; mechanism analyses point to fewer working hours, more hospital visits and weaker collaboration. The inference rests on the exclusion restriction, which the abstract does not name - common instruments (thermal inversions, upwind emissions) can also shift temperature and mobility. Annual city means are coarse against the indoor office environment where this work actually happens. Relevance: a cognitive-labour damage function in a high-exposure setting, and a case for workplace indoor monitoring rather than ambient assignment.

PAPERS.title: Fossil fuel use, urban air pollution and health in rapidly growing African cities: Implications for sustainable and low-emission urban development.
PAPERS.pm: Review of urban PM, NOx, BC and VOC evidence; source-sector attribution
PAPERS.n: PRISMA-reported critical review and policy synthesis on fossil-fuel sources, urban air quality, health impacts and governance in fast-growing African cities. Diesel road transport, backup generators and household energy emerge as the dominant PM, NOx, black carbon and VOC sources; observed levels often exceed WHO guidelines; monitoring networks are sparse and unevenly distributed. No pooled estimates, no quality appraisal of the included studies is described in the abstract, and the recommendations (electrification, clean cooking, mini-grids) are generic. Its value is as a map, not as evidence. The monitoring-gap finding is the direct link to this watch: generator-dominated diurnal profiles and diesel BC are two conditions where uncorrected optical sensors are least reliable, so an African LCS rollout needs co-located BC or reference anchors from the start.

PAPERS.title: Which Roads Should Cities Control First? A Health-Risk Framework for Mobile-Source Air Pollution.
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - road-segment mobile-source pollution with a health-risk weighting
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: ACS deposited title, authors (Ding, Zhang, Li, Chen, Hu) and DOI on 22 Sep without an abstract, and none was recoverable from Crossref, Europe PMC or PubMed. The title promises a prioritisation framework that ranks road segments by population health risk rather than by emissions alone - squarely the question a near-road sensor network is built to answer. Nothing about pollutants, exposure model, city or validation can be stated from the deposit, and inferring a method from a title is not something this watch does. Placed on the retry list; re-screen on its merits when the abstract appears, and check whether the risk weights use measured or modelled concentrations.

PAPERS.title: Determinants of early-life household air pollution exposure (HAP): carbon monoxide (CO) and PM2.5 concentrations in Bukavu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
PAPERS.pm: 24-h household PM2.5 by PurpleAir Zen; 24-h personal CO by Lascar EL-USB-CO
PAPERS.n: MUTOTO pregnancy-cohort sub-study, 405 households, March 2025 to January 2026. Mean 24-h household PM2.5 was 53.8 ug/m3 (SD 34.2), maximum household mean 244.3; personal CO averaged 5.3 ppm (SD 8.7), maximum 65.1. Biomass fuel and cooking frequency drove both; 96% of kitchens had no chimney, and biomass use rose from 56% to 87% across CO exposure groups. The limitation is metrological: PurpleAir optical counts in dense biomass smoke are not reported as corrected, and uncorrected PMS sensors typically overestimate in smoke while underestimating coarse mass - the reported means could be biased in either direction without a gravimetric subsample. Single 24-h samples also cannot capture seasonal variability. For this watch it is the model deployment: low-cost PM plus CO loggers at cohort scale in a setting with no reference network.

PAPERS.title: Chemical and toxicological assessment of particulate matter in a charcoal barbecue restaurant.
PAPERS.pm: Simultaneous indoor/outdoor PM10 filters: ions, OC/EC, organic speciation, OP (AA, DTT)
PAPERS.n: Indoor and outdoor PM10 sampled over six working days plus a closure period at one charcoal-grill restaurant. Indoor PM10 exceeded outdoor on every working day, carbonaceous matter reached half the mass, and K+, sulphate, nitrate and chloride dominated the ions; saccharides and cholesterol were the main organic tracers. Indoor extracts had higher DTT oxidative potential, lowered A549 viability and raised intracellular ROS, and ROS correlated with indoor phenolics and carboxylic acids. The design is a single site with a handful of filter days, so the correlations are descriptive, and PM10 rather than PM2.5 blurs the combustion fraction. No worker personal sampling. The chemical profile is the useful output for sensing: biomass-like K+ and cholesterol from grilling is exactly the mixed smoke-and-cooking aerosol that optical sensors misread without source-specific correction.

PAPERS.title: Health effects of indoor environmental quality (IEQ): A systematic review of indoor environments in high-income settings.
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - indoor environmental quality parameters (scope not recoverable)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: Elsevier deposited title, authors and DOI on 22 Sep with no abstract, and none was recoverable from any leg. A systematic review of IEQ health effects in high-income settings would cover indoor PM alongside thermal, acoustic, lighting and ventilation parameters, but the deposit does not say which exposures, how many studies, or whether any pooling was done, and the author list is not evidence about content either. Carried as a placeholder because indoor PM is the dominant fraction of personal exposure in high-income settings; added to the retry list and to be re-screened rather than summarised from the title.

PAPERS.title: Coated or chewable Aspirin and a hybrid air pollution mitigation strategy in patients with atherosclerotic disease: Rationale and Design of the COATED-AIR Randomized Trial.
PAPERS.pm: Real-time ambient air-quality alerts driving behavioural and KN95 responses
PAPERS.geo: Not stated (design paper; sites not in abstract)
PAPERS.n: Design paper for a 2x2 factorial randomised trial in patients with established ASCVD on low-dose aspirin: double-blind enteric-coated versus chewable aspirin 81 mg, and a hybrid air-pollution mitigation package versus usual care. The package combines an educational flashcard, SMS air-quality alerts, and on high-pollution days advice to limit outdoor activity or wear a KN95 mask and to raise citrus intake. No results. This is among the first outcome-powered trials of individual-level pollution mitigation, which is why it is tier B despite having no data. The weakness is built in: a bundled behavioural intervention cannot attribute any benefit to exposure reduction unless adherence and personal exposure are measured, which the abstract does not describe. The alert signal presumably comes from a monitoring network, so alert latency and spatial resolution are unreported design parameters.

PAPERS.title: Joint association of PM2.5 and AIP with advanced Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic syndrome in middle-aged and older Chinese adults: a national cohort study.
PAPERS.pm: Satellite-derived residential PM2.5 split at the median
PAPERS.n: CHARLS 2011-2015 participants classified by median PM2.5 and median atherogenic index of plasma, logistic regression for advanced (stage 3-4) cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome. High AIP was strongly associated; PM2.5 alone showed no positive association; joint high-PM2.5 and high-AIP exposure raised risk, with no additive or multiplicative interaction. Effect sizes and n are not in the abstract. The analysis is a median split of both exposures, so the 'joint' effect is almost entirely the AIP effect restated, and absence of interaction contradicts the framing. Preprint, not peer-reviewed. Carried for the null PM2.5 main effect, which is informative in a cohort with a wide exposure range, and as a caution against dichotomising a continuous exposure that sensor and satellite products now resolve finely.

PAPERS.title: The chemical exposome during peri-pregnancy, maternal sleep outcomes post-pregnancy, and the potential mediating role of body mass index.
PAPERS.pm: Estimated air-pollutant mixture during pregnancy within a 52-marker chemical exposome
PAPERS.n: About 393 PROGRESS mothers with 52 exposure markers (estimated air pollutants, metals, phthalates, pesticides, PFAS) in pregnancy or one month postpartum, and actigraphy plus NIH-Toolbox sleep outcomes eight years later. BWQS regression: a quartile rise in the air-pollutant mixture associated with about 8 minutes shorter sleep (beta -0.14 h, 95% CrI -0.29 to 0.00); non-essential metals lowered sleep efficiency (-0.95%, -1.81 to -0.17). No BMI mediation. The air-pollution result sits on the null boundary, the mixture's PM2.5 share is not separable in the abstract, and a single pregnancy exposure window is asked to explain sleep eight years later, over which residential and occupational exposure will have moved. Hypothesis-generating. The long lag is where repeated personal-sensor exposure histories would add the most.

PAPERS.title: Systematic misclassification of lung function in Indian adolescents using GLI-2012 reference equations: evidence from the multicity APEAL cohort.
PAPERS.pm: None at this analysis stage (APEAL air-pollution cohort baseline)
PAPERS.geo: Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Mysuru, India
PAPERS.n: Baseline of the Air Pollution Exposure on Adolescents' Lungs cohort: 4,175 healthy non-smoking 11-14-year-olds with ATS/ERS spirometry in four cities. Against GLI-2012 (Asian category), mean z-scores were -2.44 for FEV1, -1.34 for FVC and -0.78 for FEV1/FVC; 74.6% fell below the LLN for FEV1 against an expected 5%. The shift was uniform across sex, city, age, height and BMI. No PM analysis yet. It is carried because it bears directly on the outcome metrology of every South Asian PM-lung study: using GLI-2012 would label most exposed and unexposed adolescents abnormal, compressing contrasts and inflating 'impairment' prevalence. The counter-risk is that part of the deficit is itself pollution-driven, so a local reference set derived from these same cities may absorb the very effect later analyses seek.

PAPERS.title: Risk factors for allergic rhinitis in children: an umbrella review of systematic review and meta-analysis.
PAPERS.pm: Air pollution as one of 75 pooled risk factors (metric not specified in abstract)
PAPERS.n: PROSPERO-registered umbrella review of meta-analyses to May 2025, AMSTAR and GRADE appraisal. Of 75 candidate risk factors, 22 raised paediatric allergic-rhinitis risk, 7 were protective and 46 were indeterminate; air pollution sits among the risk-raising factors with antibiotics, caesarean delivery and prenatal smoking. Evidence quality was low or very low overall, and only early-life food sensitisation reached moderate certainty - so air pollution is on the list at low certainty. Pollutant, metric and pooled effect size are not given in the abstract. Umbrella reviews inherit the heterogeneity of their inputs, and ambient-pollution meta-analyses in children pool incomparable exposure assignments. A calibration of how weak the paediatric AR evidence is, not a new estimate.

PAPERS.title: Ozone and PM2.5 co-exposure exacerbates allergic rhinitis and is associated with PPAR/TRPV1-related barrier damage: Insights from nasal transcriptomic and microbial analyses.
PAPERS.pm: Acute high-dose PM2.5 and O3, single and combined, in OVA-sensitised mice
PAPERS.n: C57BL/6J allergic-rhinitis mice in five groups (control, AR, AR+O3, AR+PM2.5, AR+PM2.5+O3). Co-exposure markedly aggravated sneezing, disrupted nasal mucosa and lowered ZO-1 and occludin; nasal transcriptomics implicated PPAR/TRPV1 signalling and 16S sequencing showed microbial dysbiosis correlated with inflammation and barrier injury. The authors state the doses were acute and high and not designed to model environmental exposure, which is the limitation - interaction at high dose need not persist at ambient levels, and group sizes and PM dose are not reported in the abstract. Associations between omics layers are correlational. Carried for the co-exposure design: O3 and PM2.5 peak in different seasons in most airsheds, so their joint effect is a question sensor networks measuring both can actually address.

PAPERS.title: Mechanistic Study of SRSF1-Mediated Inhibition of Treg Cell Function via the mTORC1/ULK1 Signalling Axis Through Mitophagy in Asthma.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 instillation arm added to OVA asthma model (dose not reported in abstract)
PAPERS.n: SRSF1 was elevated in BALF cells from asthma patients and correlated negatively with Treg FOXP3 and FEV1 %pred. In OVA-asthma mice, SRSF1 upregulation in Tregs increased mTOR and ULK1-Ser757 phosphorylation and impaired mitophagy and metabolic reprogramming; SRSF1 knockdown or rapamycin restored Treg function and reduced airway inflammation, while an mTORC1 activator reversed the rescue. A PM2.5 arm exaggerated these changes in an SRSF1-dependent way. PM is secondary to the paper's question: dose, particle source and exposure route are absent from the abstract, and patient numbers are not given. The value is mechanistic - a Treg mitophagy axis through which PM could worsen established asthma - and it adds nothing to exposure-response. Tier C.

PAPERS.title: A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis on the Impact of airborne Particulate Matter on Trophoblast Cell Function In Vitro.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 extracts applied to trophoblast cell lines across 12 in vitro studies
PAPERS.n: Twelve in vitro studies from 1,506 records to September 2025. PM2.5 reduced trophoblast viability by a pooled 20.7%, disrupted steroidogenic enzymes (CYP11A1, 3beta-HSD1, FDXR), uncoupled hCG from progesterone synthesis, induced oxidative DNA damage with ATR-mediated p53-independent apoptosis, suppressed VEGF-VEGFR2-MEK-ERK-mTOR signalling and impaired invasion via TIMP, RhoA and collagen I. The central problem is that pooling relative risks of gene expression across studies with different particle sources, extraction methods, doses and cell lines produces a number with no exposure meaning; the dose axis is absent from the abstract, and cell-line trophoblasts are not placenta. Google Scholar as a search source compromises reproducibility. Useful as a pathway catalogue for placental mechanisms behind birth-weight associations, not as quantitative evidence.

PAPERS.title: Real-time monitoring of ultrafine aerosol size distributions using parallel non-bouncing impactors coupled with corona charger.
PAPERS.pm: Particle number size distribution 10-560 nm; total PNC and UFP (PM0.1)
PAPERS.n: A Parallel Electro-inertial Particle Sizer: unipolar corona charger feeding six parallel non-bouncing impactor/Faraday-cup electrometer channels with kernel inversion, 10-560 nm. Impactor cut-offs landed within 5% of design; against an SMPS, unimodal and bimodal distributions over 1e4-1e7 /cm3 were reproduced with under 10% deviation in total PNC, NMAD and GSD. In a 16-day rooftop co-location, total PNC and UFP gave slope 1.023 and r 0.995, and nucleation, growth and plume events were resolved. Weak points are stated: sub-20 nm and complex multimodal structure deviate, and one site over 16 days says nothing about drift, humidity or long-term electrometer zero stability. Cost is claimed lower but not quantified. Directly relevant: a cheaper, maintenance-light sizer is what UFP network monitoring currently lacks.

PAPERS.title: Apportioning light absorption of ambient aerosols to black carbon, brown carbon, and lensing effect using a PAX-ISS hybrid method: insights into absorption enhancement.
PAPERS.pm: Photoacoustic absorption (PAX) plus solvent-mediated integrating-sphere absorption of ambient filter samples
PAPERS.n: Couples photoacoustic spectroscopy (total, coated absorption) with an integrating sphere after solvent mediation (lensing-free absorption); the difference is the lensing term, and a dual-wavelength iteration splits the remainder into BC and BrC. Across seasonal Beijing samples in 2023, BC dominated absorption and BrC contributed about 10% annually. Lensing averaged 40% of total absorption but ranged 4.6-52.0% by season and contracted at short wavelengths, consistent with a BrC 'blocking' effect previously only simulated; annual absorption enhancement was 1.69 +/- 0.10. The assumption to test is that solvent mediation removes coatings without altering BC morphology or extracting chromophores unevenly - the method's validity rests on it. One city, one year. For low-cost absorption sensing, a seasonally varying 40% lensing term is the correction a filter photometer's mass-absorption cross-section silently absorbs.

PAPERS.title: Online characterisation of oxidative potential and reactive oxygen species of fresh and aged aircraft turbine and ship engine particulate emissions.
PAPERS.pm: Online OP and particle-bound ROS of fresh and photochemically aged aircraft-turbine and ship-engine exhaust
PAPERS.n: Only a one-sentence abstract was deposited: fresh and aged transport-sector particles from shipping and aircraft contribute significantly to particle oxidative potential. The title establishes the design - online (not filter-offline) OP and ROS measurement of fresh and aged turbine and marine-engine emissions - but no OP values, ageing conditions, fuels or particle metrics can be stated. Carried at tier B for the method: online OP is the toxicity-relevant metric a sensor network cannot yet measure, and fresh-versus-aged contrasts determine whether near-source mass is a fair proxy for harm. Retry list for the full abstract.

PAPERS.title: Vertical and Zonal Characteristics of Transatlantic Biomass Burning Aerosol Transport During the Extreme 2023 Canadian Wildfire Season.
PAPERS.pm: NAAPS reanalysis smoke AOD (550 nm), MODIS fire and AOD, modelled plume injection heights
PAPERS.n: May-September 2023 smoke transport from Canada to Europe against a 2003-2022 baseline. Source-region smoke AOD was the highest on record in every month except August. At source the 0-2 km layer held 78-93% of smoke over western Canada; during transport most smoke rose above 2 km, the 2-5 km layer dominated over the Atlantic and the extinction-weighted mean altitude climbed from 1-2 km to 2.5-4.3 km. Monthly transport efficiency to Europe was low, and satellite AOD did not reproduce the reanalysis zonal pattern. Monthly means mask episodes, and a reanalysis is not an observation. The surface-exposure implication is the useful part: when smoke is elevated, column AOD overstates surface PM2.5, so AOD-to-surface products need vertical-profile correction, and surface sensors are the check.

PAPERS.title: Demand or Congestion? Disentangling Event-Related Emissions Using a Directional Control on I-15.
PAPERS.pm: Link-level CO2, NOx and PM2.5 emissions estimated from one-minute freeway detector data
PAPERS.n: One-minute freeway detector data from the LATTICE platform during the 2026 Electric Daisy Carnival. Northbound (arrival) lost 9.5 mph over a five-hour window; southbound lost nothing, yet CO2 rose almost equally in both directions (+11.6% vs +11.8%), so the headline increase is weekend demand, not congestion. Using the uncongested direction as control in a difference-in-differences, only PM2.5 kept a substantial congestion residual (+8.9 percentage points), and residuals ranked by low-speed emission sensitivity (Spearman rho 1.00, n = 4). Emissions are modelled from speed and volume, not measured, so the PM2.5 result inherits the emission model's low-speed factors; n = 4 pollutants makes rho uninformative. Preprint. The control-corridor logic transfers directly to near-road sensor pairs.

PAPERS.title: Heterogeneous Nitrate Radical Oxidation of Catechol Produces Nitrocatechols, Oligomers, and Brown Carbon.
PAPERS.pm: Condensed-phase products of NO3 oxidation of catechol thin films (FTIR, UV-vis, ESI-MS, UHPLC-MS)
PAPERS.n: Flagged backfill: Crossref created this DOI on 20 Aug; it reached this window via a 22 Sep Europe PMC deposit and had not been carried or rejected. Catechol thin films oxidised by NO3 under dry conditions produced nitroaromatic IR bands near 1590 and 1350 cm-1, a broad UV-vis absorption centred near 349 nm characteristic of brown carbon, and 4-nitrocatechol, dinitrocatechols, dimers and trimers; the proposed route runs through semiquinone radicals, then nitration and radical coupling. Thin films under dry conditions are far from real humid particles, and no yields or mass absorption efficiencies are given, so atmospheric significance is asserted rather than shown. Paired with the PAX-ISS record in this issue: nighttime BrC formation is one source of the seasonal BrC term that record apportions.
